description: DIPPR-form temperature-dependent correlations for liquids and vapours

equationForms.100: Y = A + B T + C T^2 + D T^3 + E T^4
equationForms.101: Y = exp(A + B/T + C ln T + D T^E)
equationForms.106: Y = A (1 - Tr)^(B + C Tr + D Tr^2 + E Tr^3)   [needs Tc]

liquidViscosity.suspectReason: 18 % below CoolProp at Tr 0.85, but CoolProp's propylene viscosity is an extended-corresponding-states model (Huber et al., Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 2003), not a reference correlation, so the gap cannot be attributed. Check against a measured data set before relying on it.

liquidViscosity.suspectReason: Deviates 19-49 % from CoolProp across its entire tabulated range, while n-butane and n-hexane from the same table stay within 2 %. The coefficient structure also differs from its homologues (C3 positive, C1 an order of magnitude larger). Treat as a bad source record; substitute a measured value or use n-hexane scaled by molar mass for screening work.
